speaker: Doctor
text:
Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. You've mentioned a chronic cough, weight loss, and generalized weakness; can you tell me exactly how long you have been coughing and whether you have noticed any blood in your sputum?

REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray
REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest_X-Ray: Diffuse infiltrates; Complete_Blood_Count: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text:
The Chest X-ray shows diffuse infiltrates while your blood count is normal. To determine if this is due to an infection, autoimmune process, or malignancy like lymphoma, have you experienced any fever, night sweats, or shortness of breath?

REQUEST TEST: ESR (Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate)
REQUEST TEST: Tumor_Markers

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: ESR (Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate): NORMAL READINGS; Tumor_Markers: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text:
The ESR and tumor markers are normal, which makes active infection or overt malignancy less likely. To differentiate between interstitial lung disease and other causes, have you noticed a dry cough that worsens with exercise, or have you ever smoked?

REQUEST TEST: Pulmonary_Function_Tests
REQUEST IMAGES: HRCT_Chest

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Pulmonary_Function_Tests: NORMAL READINGS; HRCT_Chest: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text:
Good news, the pulmonary function tests and HRCT chest are both normal, which rules out significant lung parenchymal disease or obstruction. Given your chronic cough, weight loss, and weakness with otherwise normal imaging and labs, have you experienced any difficulty swallowing, regurgitation of undigested food, or heartburn?

REQUEST TEST: Upper GI Series
REQUEST TEST: 24_Hour_pH_Immittance_Monitoring

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Upper GI Series: NORMAL READINGS; 24_Hour_pH_Immittance_Monitoring: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text:
The upper GI series and pH monitoring are both normal, effectively ruling out GERD and structural esophageal issues. With normal lung imaging, labs, and GI workup, could you describe the nature of your cough, such as whether it is barking, honking, or accompanied by a sensation of a foreign body?

REQUEST TEST: Thyroid_Function_Tests
REQUEST TEST: Serum_Calcium

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Thyroid_Function_Tests: NORMAL READINGS; Serum_Calcium: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text:
The thyroid function and calcium levels are normal, which helps rule out hypocalcemia or thyroid-related causes for your cough. Since your lungs, esophagus, and blood work have all been normal, have you noticed any tremors, palpitations, or anxiety alongside your weakness?

REQUEST TEST: Serum_Potassium
REQUEST TEST: Serum_Magnesium

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Serum_Potassium: NORMAL READINGS; Serum_Magnesium: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text:
The potassium and magnesium levels are normal, ruling out common electrolyte causes for your weakness and cough. Given the chronic nature of your symptoms with normal chest, GI, and metabolic workups, have you noticed any muscle twitching, muscle pain, or difficulty walking?

REQUEST TEST: Creatine_Kinase
REQUEST TEST: Vitamin_D_Level

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Creatine_Kinase: NORMAL READINGS; Vitamin_D_Level: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text:
The creatine kinase and vitamin D levels are normal, so we can rule out primary neuromuscular disorders and vitamin deficiency as the cause of your weakness and cough. Given that your respiratory, gastrointestinal, metabolic, and muscular systems have all been cleared, have you noticed any recent changes in your stool habits, such as diarrhea, constipation, or blood in the stool?

REQUEST TEST: Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (CMP)
REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_CT

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (CMP): NORMAL READINGS; Abdominal_CT: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text:
With the CMP and abdominal CT also normal, we have effectively ruled out significant metabolic, abdominal, or structural causes for your symptoms. Have you noticed any changes in your bowel habits, such as alternating diarrhea and constipation, or any blood in your stool?

REQUEST TEST: Fecal_Impact_Check (Digital_Rectal_Exam)
REQUEST TEST: Celiac_Serology

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Fecal_Impact_Check: NORMAL READINGS; Celiac_Serology: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Idiopathic Chronic Cough with Non-Specific Generalized Weakness.

Given the exhaustive negative workup for pulmonary, gastrointestinal, metabolic, infectious, malignant, and neuromuscular causes, the clinical picture is consistent with a functional or psychogenic etiology for the cough, while the weakness may be multifactorial or related to chronic fatigue syndrome. No specific organic disease has been identified to date.
